html:
The Wik are a group of Aboriginal Australian peoples of the western Cape York Peninsula in Queensland, around today's Aurukun. They speak several related Wik languages. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Their coast saw some of the first European visitors to Australia. In 1606 the Dutch ship Duyfken sailed down this shore and turned back at Cape Keerweer, in Wik country, after clashes in which some of its crew were killed. This was the first recorded European landing in Australia. Another Dutch captain, Jan Carstenszoon, came in 1623 and also fought with the people he met.

A Presbyterian mission opened at Aurukun in 1904. The Wik are best known today for the Wik case of 1996, in which the High Court of Australia ruled that native title could survive on land held under pastoral leases. It followed the Mabo decision of 1992. Neighbours on the map include the Thaayorre and the Kaantju. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
